policy: Research-ready is not graph-ready. Staged candidates require explicit one-by-one approval after live duplicate review, source readback, relationship contracts, and a metric decision.

candidates.ontology_reason: Food insecurity is an access-and-experience construct; undernutrition is a separate biological health outcome and must not be collapsed into the same node.
candidates.repository_readback: Neither food_insecurity nor undernutrition_burden exists in the live export. The report assumption that food_insecurity already exists was rejected after live readback.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: Conflict, affordability, climate hazards, public support, and household vulnerability make attribution strongly context dependent.

staged_metric_contract.metric_name: Prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity
staged_metric_contract.transformation: Retain provider estimates and uncertainty; do not combine food insecurity with biological undernutrition outcomes.
staged_metric_contract.uncertainty: Survey and model uncertainty varies by country and release; the provider may revise historical estimates.
staged_metric_contract.threshold_provenance: FAO SDG 2.1.2 reporting and SDG target framing; no ad hoc percentile threshold.
staged_metric_contract.failure_behavior: Freeze the last reviewed release, mark stale, and never interpret a missing country-year as zero.

candidates.follow_up: Stage food_insecurity only. Keep undernutrition_burden deferred until its distinct health-state edges and double-counting rules are approved.
candidates.name: Food Insecurity
promotion_requirements: node-specific primary or official sources
at least three bounded incoming relationship contracts unless classified as an authored root
at least one meaningful downstream effect where appropriate
a complete metric contract or an explicit non-measurable rationale
manual duplicate and overlap review
candidates.rationale: The graph contains agricultural demand, crop-yield volatility, food-import exposure, price volatility, and migration, but no first-class food-insecurity or undernutrition outcome.

approval.boundary: Food insecurity only; undernutrition remains separate.

candidates.ontology_reason: The phenomenon is credible, but a broad global node blends acute disaster outcomes, chronic stress, displacement, and policy-capacity indicators.
candidates.repository_readback: No exact live node exists; overlap remains with disaster, displacement, heat-health, and health-system pathways.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: No standardized global climate-attributable mental-health burden series or production-grade observation API.
candidates.follow_up: Revisit narrower disaster-related or heat-related mental-health outcome nodes.

candidates.ontology_reason: Working-hour and earnings loss are operational consequences of occupational heat exposure, not a distinct phenomenon anchor.
candidates.repository_readback: occupational_heat_exposure exists in the live export and already represents reduced safe work capacity.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: The strongest global series is modeled and sensitive to labor-sector and work-rest assumptions.

staged_metric_contract.metric_name: Potential working hours lost due to heat exposure
staged_metric_contract.unit: hours or percent of potential working hours
staged_metric_contract.transformation: Retain modeled meteorology, labor-sector composition, work intensity, and revision version; do not treat modeled capacity loss as observed absence from work.
staged_metric_contract.uncertainty: Highly dependent on exposure assumptions, sector mix, work-rest behavior, acclimatization, and model version.
staged_metric_contract.threshold_provenance: Provider method and ILO occupational-heat framing; descriptive trend only until a universal threshold is justified.
staged_metric_contract.failure_behavior: Keep the last reviewed series and mark a methodology break instead of silently recalculating graph history.

candidates.follow_up: Implement the metric contract on occupational_heat_exposure without adding a second node.

candidates.original_name: Nutrient Pollution and Biogeochemical Flow Disruption
candidates.ontology_reason: Nutrient pollution is a measurable environmental state; biogeochemical-flow disruption is an umbrella framework spanning pressures, transport, state, and boundary exceedance.
candidates.repository_readback: No exact live node exists. Runoff, wastewater, eutrophication, algal-bloom, and hypoxia endpoints already provide a clean graph neighborhood.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: No single globally harmonized nutrient-observation API; methods and site coverage vary strongly.

staged_metric_contract.metric_name: Surface-water total nitrogen or total phosphorus concentration
staged_metric_contract.unit: milligrams per liter, tonnes per year, annual resource cost, and affected-system count reported separately
staged_metric_contract.geography: monitoring site or watershed for concentrations; worldwide UNEP assessment boundary for accumulated impact
staged_metric_contract.cadence: monthly monitoring snapshot with annual summaries and global assessment reviews
staged_metric_contract.transformation: Normalize analyte, fraction, method, units, and QA flags before watershed aggregation; for global impact retain reactive-nitrogen loss, cost, eutrophication inventories and time boundaries separately.
staged_metric_contract.uncertainty: Site coverage, method changes, detection limits and sampling frequency affect concentration trends; global nitrogen budgets combine multiple pathways and coastal inventories are monitoring-dependent lower bounds.
staged_metric_contract.threshold_provenance: Jurisdiction-specific nutrient criteria for local observations and UNEP Global Partnership on Nutrient Management assessments for global accumulated impact.
staged_metric_contract.failure_behavior: Withhold local aggregation when method or site coverage is insufficient; retain the last reviewed global assessment and never extrapolate a US concentration, convert site count to area, or allocate a global cost to one watershed.

candidates.follow_up: Stage with US-only measurement scope first; require separate relationship dossiers before live promotion.

promotion_requirements: node-specific primary or official sources
at least three bounded incoming relationship contracts unless classified as an authored root
at least one meaningful downstream effect where appropriate
a complete metric contract or an explicit non-measurable rationale
manual duplicate and overlap review
candidates.rationale: Fertilizer runoff, manure, wastewater, eutrophication, harmful algal blooms, hypoxia, and fishery impacts exist as fragments without a nitrogen-phosphorus system anchor.

approval.boundary: Nutrient state only; not an umbrella biogeochemical-flow score.

candidates.original_name: Toxic Chemical Pressure and Novel Entities
candidates.ontology_reason: The label combines releases, occurrence, exposure, hazard, persistence, and regulatory status without a defensible common unit or weighting rule.
candidates.repository_readback: Several narrower chemical, plastics, pesticide, and contamination nodes exist; the umbrella would obscure rather than repair those pathways.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: No scientifically stable aggregate metric across heterogeneous substances and hazard dimensions.
candidates.follow_up: Research narrower daughters such as toxic_chemical_releases, PFAS contamination, or plastic pollution.

candidates.ontology_reason: Seagrass is a distinct habitat state with specific carbon, nursery, water-quality, and shoreline functions.
candidates.repository_readback: No exact live node exists. It is distinct from coral, mangrove, saltmarsh, kelp, and generic blue-carbon loss nodes.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: Comparable global area-change baselines are episodic and sensitive to mapping era and method.

staged_metric_contract.metric_name: Mapped seagrass meadow area change from baseline
staged_metric_contract.transformation: Use curated habitat polygons for area change; use OBIS occurrences only for supporting QA and never as evidence of absence.
staged_metric_contract.uncertainty: Mapping era, classification method, seasonal cover, and incomplete remapping limit comparability.
staged_metric_contract.threshold_provenance: Persistent decline across at least two comparable mapping periods; no occurrence-only threshold.
staged_metric_contract.failure_behavior: Do not update area change from raw occurrences; retain the prior polygon snapshot with its mapping uncertainty.

candidates.follow_up: Stage snapshot-first. OBIS may support QA but must not drive area-loss scoring from presence-only records.

candidates.rationale: Mangroves, coral reefs, kelp, and generic blue-carbon habitat loss are present, but seagrass is absent despite distinct drivers and ecosystem functions.

approval.boundary: Mapped habitat decline; occurrences are supporting evidence only.

candidates.ontology_reason: Urban heat island is the phenomenon; intensity in degrees Celsius is its primary metric, not a second node.
candidates.repository_readback: urban_heat_island does not exist in the live export. urban_heat_dome_stagnation is not an ontology duplicate, so the report merge assumption was rejected.
candidates.largest_uncertainty: A globally comparable series requires a fixed urban footprint, rural reference, retrieval method, and day/night definition.

staged_metric_contract.transformation: Keep surface and canopy-layer UHI separate; retain urban footprint, rural reference, day/night, season, and sensor or model version.
staged_metric_contract.uncertainty: Urban-boundary choice, elevation, morphology, weather, land-cover change, and retrieval method affect comparability.
staged_metric_contract.threshold_provenance: Provider-defined urban-minus-reference method and health-relevance literature; no arbitrary global percentile.
staged_metric_contract.failure_behavior: Freeze the prior value when footprint or processing changes cannot be back-cast.

candidates.follow_up: Stage the phenomenon with intensity as its metric; do not conflate it with urban heat dome stagnation.
